item.title: I Gave My Life Over to Meta’s A.I. Agent and Was Blown Away
item.description: Muse, Meta’s A.I. agent, helped handle my dental insurance, booked dinner reservations and created a podcast for me. It also required my most personal data, and trust.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Poppy Lynch for The New York Times
item.media:description: The New York Times reporter Eli Tan using Meta Muse to buy movie tickets in San Francisco.

item.title: An A.I. Image of Trump Kissing a Woman Was Fake. It Spread Anyway.
item.description: Advances in artificial intelligence and the myriad ways content is shared online have made establishing authenticity even more difficult for users of social media.
item.dc:creator: Steven Lee Myers, Tiffany Hsu and Stuart A. Thompson
item.media:credit: The New York Times

item.title: Anthropic Releases a New A.I. Model, Opus 5.5, Amid Safety Debate
item.description: The company released a cheaper, faster model that it said was the strongest performer on its most rigorous internal safety tests to date.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Eric Helgas for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anthropic’s new artificial intelligence model, Opus 5.5, was the first release since the company’s chief executive called for the industry to slow down.

item.title: What to Know About Recent A.I. Hacks at Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta
item.description: OpenAI, Google and others recently disclosed breaches by their artificial intelligence models that amplified concerns about the advancing capabilities of the technology.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: An analysis of one recent hack by OpenAI technology helped to reveal how A.I. agents communicated with one another.

item.title: An Army of Paid Creators Is Carpeting the Web With Political Content
item.description: Unlike celebrity influencers with large followings, these creators produce a blizzard of videos for a fraction of the cost of traditional online campaigns and, in the process, shift public conversation.
item.dc:creator: Ken Bensinger and Stuart A. Thompson
item.media:credit: The New York Times

item.title: The Big Threat Has Been Climate Change. Now Comes A.I.
item.description: Both are human-caused, both are frightening, and one of them has raced to the forefront of the global conversation.
item.dc:creator: Chico Harlan
item.media:credit: Brandon Bell/Getty Images
item.media:description: Construction of an A.I. data center in Texas last month.

item.title: How to Split Expenses on a Group Trip Without Fighting
item.description: From bachelorette trips to family vacations, group travel can cause relationship-ending fallouts. Here’s how to navigate difficult conversations about finances.
item.dc:creator: Ryley Ober
item.media:credit: Matthew Kam

item.title: As Computers Take the Driver’s Seat, Experts Worry About Safety
item.description: Self-driving systems are getting so good that drivers may overestimate the technology and not be prepared to respond when something goes wrong.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.media:credit: Erin Schaff/The New York Times
item.media:description: Hands-free driving in a Rivian. The automaker is among those offering systems that allow drivers to take their hands off the steering wheel on certain roads.

item.title: How Potential 2028 Presidential Candidates Are Talking About A.I.
item.description: Democrats are jockeying to embrace new safeguards, while Republicans have aligned with President Trump’s warnings against slowing down the technology.
item.dc:creator: Evan Gorelick
item.media:credit: Allison Robbert for The New York Times

item.title: The A.I. Party House Where Networking Has a Dark Side
item.description: Group tech houses have proliferated across the San Francisco Bay Area in the artificial intelligence boom. One of the most prominent has also racked up an extensive police record.
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Grind
item.media:credit: Minh Connors for The New York Times
item.media:description: The entrance to AGI House in Hillsborough, Calif. AGI House is one of the most prominent and notorious tech group homes in the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Gemini AI Hacked Three Companies in a Testing Breakout, Google Says
item.description: A third-party test company inadvertently gave internet access to Google’s Gemini and other artificial intelligence models during cybersecurity testing.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Andria Lo for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Gemini incidents occurred while the model was undergoing testing at Irregular, an Israeli start-up that works with tech companies to assess their A.I. models before they are publicly released.

item.title: Anthropic Pursues IPO Despite Its A.I. Safety Warnings
item.description: The company is expected to reach $100 billion in annualized revenue this year, even as chief executive Dario Amodei calls for slowing down development of some advanced A.I. models.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Hirsch, Sri Muppidi, Erin Griffith and Mike Isaac
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, is said to have met with potential investors in the company’s blockbuster I.PO. in recent weeks.

item.title: Uber to Pay $40 Million to Parents of Woman Fatally Hit by Car
item.description: Emily Normandin-Parker, 23, was struck and killed on a California freeway after an Uber driver ordered her and a friend out of his car in August 2023.
item.dc:creator: Christine Hauser
item.media:credit: Jim Wilson/The New York Times
item.media:description: The case touched on the legal extent to which Uber is responsible for the actions of its drivers.

item.title: California Governor Gavin Newsom Issues A.I. Safety Executive Order
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom ordered the state to develop recommendations on safety measures, including requiring companies to build a “kill switch,” amid mounting concerns.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe
item.media:credit: Jeff Chiu/Associated Press
item.media:description: “We’re going to speed up our work on substantial and responsible A.I. oversight before it’s too late,” Gov. Gavin Newsom of California said in a news release.

item.title: Iran and China Create First-of-Their-Kind Autonomous A.I. Influence Campaigns
item.description: The countries, along with Israeli firms, combined Chinese open-source A.I. models and A.I. agents for the campaigns, foreshadowing future online manipulation.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel, Eli Tan and Dustin Volz
item.media:credit: Brian Stauffer

item.title: A.I. Safety Goes Mainstream + a ‘Hard Fork’ Exit AMA

item.title: As Big Tech Takes Over Hollywood, the Picture Onscreen Gets Darker
